get.description:
Report that the process is alive.

Deliberately touches nothing external: a database outage must not make the
orchestrator kill a process that is working fine.

Report whether the process can serve traffic.

Returns 503 when a dependency is down, so a load balancer stops sending
requests, while leaving the process running.

Describe the organisation this credential belongs to.

Reaching this endpoint at all is the proof the credential works, which is
what makes it the right thing for ``vexpath login`` to call.

Every project of the caller's organisation.

No organisation filter in the query: row-level security applies it, and
adding one here would suggest the filter is this endpoint's job rather
than the database's.

schema.title: Response List Projects V1 Projects Get

post.description:
Create a project.

The organisation comes from the credential, never from the request body. A
caller who could name the organisation could create a project inside
someone else's, and the row-level security policy would then happily let
them read it back.

get.description:
The project's current policy, so a build can apply the same rule.

Exists so that a policy configured once in the dashboard governs every
scan, rather than depending on each caller passing the right ``--policy``
flag. ``vexpath scan --policy project`` reads this.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404 if the project does not exist for this
        organisation, or if it has no policy. Those are deliberately the
        same answer: a project with no policy has nothing to apply, and
        the caller's next move is identical either way.
get.summary: Read the policy that governs a project

put.description:
Change whether a project's reports are published.

Its own endpoint rather than a field on a general update, because this is
the one setting whose effect is visible to the entire internet, and it
should be hard to change by accident while editing something else.

schema.title: Response List Scans V1 Scans Get

post.description:
Store the result of a scan run elsewhere.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404 if the project does not exist for this
        organisation, 422 if the results document is not one this build
        understands, 413 if it is implausibly large.

get.description:
Every finding of a scan, worst first.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404 if the scan does not exist for this organisation.
        The same answer whether it belongs to someone else or to nobody,
        because distinguishing them would make this a way of asking what
        other organisations have scanned.

schema.title: Response List Findings V1 Scans  Scan Id  Findings Get

get.summary: Findings of one scan, with evidence

get.description:
Every suppression of the caller's organisation.

Expired and revoked ones are left out by default and available on request.
Nothing deletes them: the record of what was suppressed and why is worth
more than a tidy table, and it is the only way to answer "how long has
this been ignored".

schema.title: Response List Suppressions V1 Suppressions Get

post.description:
Record a decision not to fix something.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404 if the project is not the caller's, 422 if the
        suppression is one this system will not record -- no reason, or a
        duration long enough that the expiry would be a formality.

delete.description:
Revoke a suppression, bringing the finding back into view.

Marked revoked rather than deleted, so the history stays: a finding that
was suppressed for five months and then was not is a different situation
from one nobody ever suppressed, and only the first is worth a
conversation.

schema.title: Response List Webhooks V1 Webhooks Get

post.description:
Register an endpoint, and return its signing secret once.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 422 for a URL this system will not connect to or an
        unknown event name, 404 if the named project is not the caller's.

delete.description:
Delete a webhook and its delivery history.

Deleted rather than marked, unlike a suppression: a webhook is a piece of
configuration rather than a decision, and nobody needs to know later that
an endpoint used to be subscribed. The audit log records that it was
removed.

get.description:
What happened on recent deliveries.

The outcome and the error, never the payload: a delivery carries findings,
and a second copy of them in a log doubles the places a leak can come
from.

schema.title: Response List Deliveries V1 Webhooks  Webhook Id  Deliveries Get

post.description:
Turn a disabled webhook back on and forget its failures.

A webhook switched off after twenty consecutive failures stays off until
somebody says the receiver is fixed. Clearing the count here is what makes
that statement, rather than the next delivery disabling it again on its
first retry.

Deliver a ``ping`` now, and return what happened.

Synchronous on purpose, unlike a real event. Somebody who has just pasted
a URL wants to know whether it works, and a test whose result arrives in a
log five minutes later is a test nobody runs.

Replace the signing secret, and return the new one once.

Exists so a leaked secret can be replaced without deleting the webhook,
which would lose its delivery history -- and the history is how somebody
works out whether the leak was used.
